3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.171 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) I.P.C. and 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station- Chiluwatal, District- Gorakhpur, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 15 years on 19.3.2024 at about 11:50 p.m.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. The FIR is delayed by about one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
7. The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., whereby she has stated that she was having corporeal relationship with the applicant for about three years and she has expressed her willingness to stay with the applicant only.
She has also stated that she had left her house on her own.

8. The victim by her physical appearance seems to be major, although she has told her age to be 17 years in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
9.
The applicant is ready to take care of the victim and her offspring and marry her after his release from jail.
10. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
11. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 21.3.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/OPPOSITE PARTY 12.

The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the informant has refused to take the notice and has also refused to take care of her daughter, as such the victim is staying in a women shelter home.
She has been left to lead a life of destitution.
She has nowhere to go.

CONCLUSION:
13. It is an admitted fact that the victim and the applicant had corporeal relationship out of consent.
The counsel for applicant has undertaken that applicant is ready to take care of the victim and her offspring and marry her after his release from jail.
14.
The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

15. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life Baliram vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67239707/
2 or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
16.

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
17. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
18. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

19. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the said statement of counsel for applicant that applicant is ready to take care of the victim and the offspring borne out of the said corporeal relationship, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

20. Let the applicant- Baliram involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant after his release from jail shall marry the victim within a period of three months.
(ii) The applicant shall deposit (fixed deposit) a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- in the account opened in the name of the victim within a period of six months from the date of his release from jail.
(iii) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
